subtopic: Deadlock Detection, Prevention and Race Conditions
question_text: What does a Memory Barrier (or Memory Fence) instruction enforce in CPU execution pipelines?

options.text: Enforces strict ordering constraints on memory operations before and after the fence, preventing hardware out-of-order reordering
Protects kernel memory space from user space writes
Causes immediate context switching to another thread

answer_explanation: CPUs reorder instructions for performance. Memory fences guarantee that all read/write operations preceding the fence complete before any operations following it are committed.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: CPUs reorder instructions for performance. Memory fences guarantee that all read/write operations preceding the fence complete before any operations following it are committed.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
